title: UniPoolerV2 'Overflow bound' NatSpec still justifies _swapAmount's checked product by uint112 reserves and a balance cap, neither of which holds for quotePool after 267660b
description: The 'Overflow bound' NatSpec bounds _swapAmount's checked product with two claims: 'V2 reserves are uint112' and 'a is capped by this contract's sUSDS balance'. After 267660b, quotePool feeds _swapAmount uint256 balanceOf(pair) values (:502, :531-533), not uint112 reserves. quotePool also never caps sUSDSIn by the contract balance (its own @dev says it can quote hypothetical amounts), so the second claim has never held for quotePool. pool() still satisfies both: sync() reverts above uint112, and :459 caps a.
impact: None. The comment is wrong, but the arithmetic is checked, so an out-of-range input reverts instead of wrapping.
likelihood: n/a. r^2 * ~4e6 overflows 2^256 only when r > ~1.7e35 wei (1.7e17 sUSDS), far above sUSDS supply. A pair balance above uint112 also makes pool()'s sync() revert ('UniswapV2: OVERFLOW'). A caller-supplied hypothetical sUSDSIn that overflows only reverts a view call.
severityJustification: The 'Overflow bound' NatSpec still bounds the checked product of _swapAmount by uint112 reserves and a balance-capped `a`. Since 267660b, quotePool feeds uint256 balanceOf values and an unbounded caller `a` into that product, so the stated premise no longer holds for the quote path. The conclusion that an out-of-range input reverts instead of wrapping is still true, because the multiplication is checked. Reaching the overflow region needs a pair balance about 30x above the uint112 cap and beyond total sUSDS supply. pool() itself still sizes from uint112 reserves after sync. The only effect is that a view call reverts on a hypothetical input. This is a comment-accuracy issue (QA/NC); there is no availability or value impact to support Low.
recommendation: Restate the bound per call site. pool() uses uint112 reserves after sync. quotePool uses uint256 balances and a caller `a` and can revert on absurd inputs, which is acceptable for a view.
